reviews.title: Dune: Part Two
reviews.author: Avery Durham
reviews.body: Denis Villeneuve delivers a breathtaking continuation of the Dune saga. The visuals are stunning, the performances are captivating, and the story unfolds with epic scope and intimate emotion. Timothee Chalamet rises to the occasion as Paul Atreides, and Zendaya's expanded role adds real depth. This is sci-fi filmmaking at its absolute finest.

reviews.title: Oppenheimer
reviews.author: Avery Durham
reviews.body: Christopher Nolan crafts a riveting, complex portrait of the man who changed the world forever. Cillian Murphy delivers a career-defining performance, supported by an incredible ensemble cast. The film is dense, ambitious, and deeply unsettling in the best way. A monumental achievement in biographical filmmaking.

reviews.title: The Holdovers
reviews.author: Avery Durham
reviews.body: Alexander Payne delivers a warm, funny, and quietly moving film about unexpected human connection. Paul Giamatti is wonderful as a cantankerous prep school teacher stuck over winter break with a troubled student. It feels like a modern classic, with a timeless quality and genuine heart.

reviews.title: Killers of the Flower Moon
reviews.author: Avery Durham
reviews.body: Martin Scorsese brings devastating historical gravity to this story of greed and betrayal in 1920s Oklahoma. Leonardo DiCaprio and Robert De Niro lead a powerful cast, but it is Lily Gladstone who steals the film with a quietly devastating performance. It is long, but every minute earns its place.

reviews.title: Barbie
reviews.author: Avery Durham
reviews.body: Greta Gerwig turns a toy commercial into a genuinely subversive, hilarious, and emotionally resonant film. Margot Robbie and Ryan Gosling are perfectly cast, and the production design is jaw-dropping. It is smarter and more heartfelt than anyone expected, while still being a total blast.

reviews.title: Past Lives
reviews.author: Avery Durham
reviews.body: Celine Song's debut is a profoundly beautiful meditation on love, fate, and the paths we do not take. Greta Lee and Teo Yoo deliver restrained, aching performances. The film is patient and quiet, trusting its audience to feel the weight of every glance and silence. An extraordinary first film.

reviews.title: Spider-Man: Across the Spider-Verse
reviews.author: Avery Durham
reviews.body: This sequel pushes the boundaries of animation even further than the original. The visual creativity is staggering, with each universe having its own distinct style. The story is emotionally rich, dealing with fate, identity, and sacrifice. It ends on a cliffhanger that will leave you desperate for more.

reviews.title: Poor Things
reviews.author: Avery Durham
reviews.body: Yorgos Lanthimos delivers a wildly inventive and darkly funny film anchored by a fearless Emma Stone performance. The production design is fantastical and immersive, and the film tackles big ideas about autonomy, pleasure, and what it means to be human. It is strange, beautiful, and utterly unique.
